item.title: A proof of Karp's conjecture on the zeros of Toeplitz determinants of rising factorial series
item.description: arXiv:2610.18895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2012, D. Karp studied a family of polynomials constructed from Polya frequency sequences and conjectured that all their zeros are real and negative. We prove this conjecture for positive sequences and establish further results concerning the location of these zeros.
item.dc:creator: Henry Zweiman

item.title: The zeros of point evaluation extremals in Paley-Wiener spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.19132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $1\le p < \infty$, $\varphi_p$ is the function of minimal $L^p$ norm among all functions $f$ of exponential type at most $\pi$ for which $f(0)=1$. We start from the ansatz that the positive zeros $\tau_n$ of $\varphi_p$ are close to \(n+1/p-1/2\) and use a weighted convex correction to first place them in an \(\ell^2\)-neighborhood of this sequence. A bootstrap argument then improves this to a {Poincar\'e asymptotic} expansion of $\tau_n-(n+\frac1p-\frac12)$ in terms of odd powers of $(n+\frac1p-\frac12)^{-1}$. We also get precise information about the Fourier transform $\widehat{\varphi}_p$, a result that in particular implies that for all integers $n\ge 2$, $\widehat{\varphi}_{2n}$ is an integrable function which, when convolved with itself $2n-2$ times, is constant on the interval $[-\pi,\pi]$. In particular, we identify the extremizer in an autoconvolution problem posed by B. Green in 2001.
item.dc:creator: Andriy Bondarenko, Joaquim Ortega-Cerd\`a, Kristian Seip

item.title: Sparse bounds for rough non-translation-invariant Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.19468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish sparse bounds for singular integral operators with rough non-translation-invariant Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund kernels. Our approach verifies the localized hypothesis in the sparse domination framework introduced by Conde-Alonso, Di Plinio et al. The proof refines Seeger's microlocal decomposition using a Littlewood-Paley analysis adapted to the non-translation-invariant setting. As applications, we obtain quantitative weighted estimates for Calder\'{o}n-type commutators and other singular integrals with rough kernels.
item.dc:creator: Yanping Chen, Teng Wang

item.title: Sharp radial--angular mixed norm Fourier extension and global stability on spheres

item.title: Endpoint regularity of Radon transforms associated with real analytic phases in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.19854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider the endpoint Sobolev regularity of Radon transforms associated with real-analytic functions in the plane. We establish all of the failure of endpoint regularity for real-analytic phases. On the one hand, the critical endpoint regularity $L^p(\mathbb{R}^2)\rightarrow L^p_s(\mathbb{R}^2)$, corresponding to extreme points of the reduced Newton polyhedron of phase function, is true if only and only if $p=2$. For generic extreme points, this failure of endpoint regularity generalizes a result of Christ \cite{christ}. On the other hand, we find that the endpoint Sobolev regularity also fails on a bounded segment of the reduced Newton polyhedron when the bisectrix $y=x$ intersects one of unbounded faces at a relative interior point. In particular, our results imply that the Radon transform is not bounded from $L^p$ into $L^p_{1/n}$ with $p=n/(n-1)$ or $p=n$, where the phase functions are real-valued homogeneous polynomials $S(x,y)=a_1x^{n-1}y+a_2x^{n-2}y^2+\cdots+a_{n-1}xy^{n-1}$ with $n\geq 3$ and $a_1a_{n-1}\neq0$. This answers a problem of Phong and Stein in 1994. Moreover, the main results of this paper also give examples which show failure of critical Sobolev regularity for degenerate Fourier integral operators satisfying finite type conditions formulated in \cite{Seeger93,seeger2}. Based on earlier results and our proof of several remaining cases, we conclude that all of other critical endpoint Sobolev estimates are true for Radon transforms associated with real-analytic phases in the plane. Therefore, all failures of endpoint regularity estimates are clearly determined.
item.dc:creator: Danglin Li, Zuoshunhua Shi

item.title: Elementary ratio and zero limits for varying recurrences
item.description: arXiv:2610.19930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two theorems of Loureiro and Van Assche on ratio and zero limits provided part of the motivation for this note. Their elementary nature permits direct proofs; Appendix B gives complete proofs of both for the canonical initial conditions, using earlier continued-fraction identities. We prove ratio limits and weak limits of normalized zero measures for varying higher-order three-term recurrences with arbitrary coefficient periods and independent limiting functions for their phases. Joint local coefficient limits give ratio convergence without uniform coefficient bounds. For zero measures, convergence in measure to finite measurable profiles suffices, without boundedness or integrability; the limiting measures may have noncompact support. Coefficients may vanish, and real diagonal terms are allowed for ordinary three-term recurrences. The proofs use interlacing, partial fractions with nonnegative residues, local computations of moments, and stability of zero counts under changes of recurrence coefficients. Truncation removes the coefficient bounds from the zero theorem, whose proof is independent of ratio asymptotics. Uniform bounds give the version with compact support. Power-law limits and their explicit transform formula follow as a special case.
item.dc:creator: K. Castillo, S. Yakubovich

item.title: Old structures, a vanishing formula
item.description: arXiv:2610.20192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify a normalization defect in a determinantal construction of fourth-order Hahn difference equations and compare its scalar equation with Foupouagnigni's 1998 elimination and its published 2001 counterpart. On an explicit positive orthogonal family, all five prescribed coefficients vanish: the formula gives \(0=0\) and imposes no condition. Along an explicit regular perturbation, division by \(\varepsilon^2\) before specialization recovers a nonzero equation on that family, the same scalar equation as the correctly executed old shift-and-eliminate procedure. On the common nondegenerate domain specified below, both constructions give the same scalar operator up to a nonzero rational factor. The first-order degree bounds follow directly from valid identities of 1998; preserving cancellations gives a bound that can be arbitrarily sharper on explicit admissible inputs, together with exact top coefficients and cancellation criteria. Explicit coefficient formulas do not by themselves yield a new scalar equation on this domain. Our comparison does not exclude corrective or expository contributions; additional computational gain or exceptional coverage must be demonstrated.
item.dc:creator: K. Castillo, G. Gordillo-N\'u\~nez

item.title: Characterization of $C^{1,\alpha}$-domains in terms of Carleson-type $\varepsilon$-coefficients
item.dc:creator: Xavier Tolsa, Tobias Wang

item.title: Gaussian rigidity and width of measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.20385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given $0\le m<n$ and a positive Radon measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^n$ with at most polynomial growth, assume that it has finite $m$-dimensional \emph{Gaussian discrepancy}, defined as $$\mathcal D(\mu):=\limsup_{R\to\infty}\Bigl[R^2\sup_{x\in\mathrm{spt}\mu}|G_R^\mu(x)-1|\Bigr],$$ where $G_R^\mu(x):=(4\pi R^2)^{-m/2}\int_{\mathbb R^n} e^{-|z-x|^2/(4R^2)}\,d\mu(z)$. Provided that $\mu$ admits a flat blow-down $\mathcal H^m\llcorner V$ (an assumption that cannot be dropped entirely), we prove that there exists a finite (smallest) $0\le\delta<\infty$, called the \emph{width} of $\mu$, such that $$\mathrm{spt}\mu\subseteq \bar B_\delta(V+x_0),\quad \delta^2\le C(m,n)\mathcal{D}(\mu),$$ where $\bar B_\delta(V+x_0)$ denotes the closed $\delta$-neighborhood of a suitable translate of $V$. Note that the exponent is optimal because of scale invariance. In particular, when $\mathcal D(\mu)=0$, the support of $\mu$ is included in an $m$-dimensional affine plane. We use this fact to give a simpler proof of Preiss's rectifiability theorem: while still based on Gaussian averages of $\mu$, this new proof avoids showing uniqueness (and hence conicality) of blow-downs of $m$-uniform measures, as well as studying Gaussian-weighted moments beyond second order. The strategy of proof consists of an anisotropic blow-down of $\mu$, followed by an analysis of the resulting Young measure, using a rigidity lemma involving the heat semigroup.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Pigati

item.title: Packing intermediate dimensions of measures and applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.18929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a spectrum of dimensions of measures, the \emph{packing intermediate dimensions} $\dim_{P,\theta}\mu$, $\theta\in(0,1]$, of a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and the \emph{quasi-Hausdorff dimension} $\dim_{qH}\mu$. We show that this spectrum encodes the information on $\mu$ that governs the packing dimension of its projections and H\"{o}lder images. First, $\dim_{qH}\mu$ is the exact threshold for the packing dimension profiles of Falconer and Howroyd: for every real $0<s\leq n$, $\dim_P^s\mu=s$ if and only if $s\leq\dim_{qH}\mu$. Second, we prove a lower bound for the profiles in terms of $\dim_H\mu$, $\dim_{P,\theta}\mu$ and the Assouad dimension of $\operatorname{supp}\mu$, which improves the bound of Falconer and Mattila, the best previously known general lower bound for the packing dimension of projected measures. The improvement is strict whenever $\dim_H\mu<\dim_P\mu$ and $\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}\mu)<n$, and when $\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}\mu)=n$ it occurs exactly when $\dim_{P,\theta}\mu$ exceeds an explicit universal lower bound for some $\theta$ in an explicit range. We present examples of measures with $\dim_H\mu<\dim_P\mu<\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}\mu)=n$ for which our bound gives the exact value $\dim_P\mu_V=\min\{\dim_P\mu,m\}$ for almost every $m$-dimensional subspace $V$, whereas the bound of Falconer and Mattila is strictly smaller. As applications, for a large family of random $\alpha$-H\"{o}lder maps $f_\omega:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$, we prove that, for compactly supported $\mu$, $\dim_P\mu_{f_\omega}=m$ almost surely if and only if $\alpha m\leq\dim_{qH}\mu$, and that the packing analogue of Kahane's formula holds for fractional Brownian motions if and only if $\dim_{qH}\mu=\dim_P\mu$. Analogous results are obtained for analytic sets.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Angelini

item.title: A sharp discrete Sobolev inequality and left inverses of higher order differences
item.description: arXiv:2610.19010v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For integers $\alpha,d \geqslant1$, we determine the best constants in the inequalities $||(a_j)_{j=1}^{d}||_{\ell^1} \leqslant C_{\alpha,d} ||((\Delta^\alpha a)_j)_{j=1}^{d+\alpha}||_{\ell^2},$ where $\Delta$ is the difference operator. We find that these constants correspond to the $\ell^2$ norm of the discrete Chebyshev polynomials, and show that the extremal sequences may be obtained by appropriate sampling of the discrete Landau polynomials. From beginning to end, this project was carried out without use of AI.
item.dc:creator: Raul Hindov, Shahaf Nitzan, Jan-Fredrik Olsen, Eskil Rydhe

item.title: Uniqueness of Limit Cycles for Abel Equations and Planar Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.19340v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study positive limit cycles of the Abel equation $$\dot{x}=A(t)x^{3}+B(t)x^{2},$$ where $A$ and $B$ are $2\pi$-periodic functions. By developing a half-period convexity method, we establish a new criterion ensuring that the equation has at most one positive limit cycle. Moreover, if such a limit cycle exists, it is hyperbolic. As applications, we consider two classes of planar polynomial systems that can be reduced to Abel equations. For a subfamily of cubic rigid systems, we prove that there is at most one limit cycle, thereby giving a partial answer to the first problem in Gasull's list of 33 open problems. For quadratic systems, we derive a new uniqueness criterion for limit cycles surrounding the origin and provide explicit parameter regions under which the criterion is satisfied.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Luis Bravo Trinidad, Renhao Tian, Yulin Zhao

item.title: Fractional elementary symmetric functions and Hessian estimates in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.19410v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove an endpoint Pucci maximum principle for domains in $\mathbb R^2$, formulated using a generalization of elementary symmetric polynomials to noninteger orders. As a result, we sharpen an earlier result of Astala, Iwaniec and Martin, and deduce a new Sobolev inequality for $q$-Hessians where $1 < q < 2$. The fractional elementary symmetric functions we use are derived through fractional differentiation. Their signed singular value extension coincides with the Burkholder functional introduced by Burkholder and gives us access to a local Burkholder inequality due to Astala, Iwaniec, Prause and Saksman, leading to a different proof of the Pucci maximum principle from the one in that used quasiconformal maps. We include an elementary real-variable proof of this local Burkholder inequality, obtained by combining a few known techniques from existing literature.
item.dc:creator: Gautam Neelakantan Memana, Neil S. Trudinger, Po-Lam Yung

item.title: Weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for Riesz transforms of elliptic operators and magnetic Schr\"odinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.19469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian manifold and define a magnetic Schr\"odinger operator $\LL = ({\bf d}+ iA)^*({\bf d}+iA) + V$ where $A$ is a real $1$-differential form in $L^2_{loc}$ and $V \in L^1_{loc}$ is a nonnegative electric potential. We prove that the magnetic Riesz transform $({\bf d} + iA) \LL^{-\einhalb}$ is of weak type $(1,1)$ with bound at most $2$. It extends to a bounded operator on $L^p$ for $p \in (1, 2]$ with norm bounded by a constant $c_p$ depending only on $p$. It is then independent of the dimension of the manifold and independent of $A$ and $V$. We also prove weak type $(1,1)$ bounds for symmetric elliptic operators subject to various boundary conditions on rough domains of $\RR^d$. The proofs are based on a new weak type $(1,1)$ criterion for operators.
item.dc:creator: El Maati Ouhabaz

item.title: Entire solutions of higher order Briot-Bouquet equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.20438v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a meromorphic function $f$ in the complex plane, we determine when $f$ and $f^{(k)}$ are algebraically dependent. This happens precisely when $f$ belongs to the class $W$ of elliptic functions and their degenerates, or satisfies a linear differential equation $f^{(k)} + af + b = 0$ with constant coefficients. The case of functions having a pole was settled previously. We complete the proof by treating entire solutions.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Eremenko, Tuen Wai Ng, Teng Zhang

item.title: A proof of Saari's homographic conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2212.10148v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove Saari's homographic conjecture for a large class of $n$-body problems with power law potentials, including the classical $n$-body problem.
item.dc:creator: Pieter Tibboel

item.title: An Exploration of Lacunary Orthogonal Polynomials Associated with the Geronimus Transformation
item.description: arXiv:2606.06639v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this note, we present two perturbations of sequences of orthogonal polynomials related to two iterations of the Geronimus transformation, with the feature that the resulting sequences of polynomials are missing a single degree. We relate these sequences to quasi-orthogonal polynomials of order 2 and investigate properties including recurrence relations, completeness, and associated differential equations.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Bailey, Roman Gavrilov

item.title: Estimates for $L^p$ variants of Gowers norms
item.description: arXiv:2609.08916v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by a log-convexity question of Bennett and Tao, we consider Gowers-type functionals defined by $L^p$ norms of multiple autocorrelations. We prove sharp bounds in terms of $L^q$ norms and characterise the near-extremisers on Euclidean spaces as well as locally compact abelian groups. We also establish two families of degree-lowering inequalities and study their near-extremisers. As a byproduct of this broader theory, we show that the constant in the log-convexity estimate for Gowers norms is strictly less than unity, confirming the aforementioned conjecture of Bennett and Tao. Finally, we characterise the $p$ for which the Gowers-type functionals necessarily satisfy the triangle inequality on nonnegative measurable functions.
item.dc:creator: Vjekoslav Kova\v{c}, Keith M. Rogers

item.title: The ultraspherical background of the Jacobi phase expansion, in closed form
item.description:
arXiv:2609.29531v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The large-degree phase of the Jacobi polynomial $P_n^{(\alpha, eta)}(\cos	heta)$ contains, at each order in $\Nn^{-1}$, $\Nn=n+(\alpha+ eta+1)/2$, an additive constant $\kappa_r$ that the phase equation does not determine. These constants are antisymmetric in $(\alpha^2, eta^2)$ and vanish for $\alpha= eta$. We obtain three results. First, on the diagonal $\alpha= eta$ the logarithm of the midpoint amplitude is computed in closed form: if $L_n$ denotes the coefficient of $(2\Nn)^{-n}$ in that logarithm, then $\Upsilon_A(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}L_nt^n/(n-1)!$ equals \[ \Upsilon_A(t)= rac{e^{t} igl(\cosh2\alpha t-\cosh t igr)}{\sinh 2t}. \] The proof is algebraic: the identity is established for half-odd-integer $\alpha$, where the expansion terminates, by means of two classical recurrences for Bessel polynomials, and is extended to all $\alpha$ by a degree argument. Second, the derivative of the logarithm of the amplitude with respect to $\alpha^2$ at the Legendre point $\alpha= eta=0$ is computed in closed form to all orders. An exact reduction of an Appell $F_3$ function to a Gauss function shows that it is a parameter derivative of a zero-balanced ${}_2F_1$ at argument $2$; the real part of its expansion is a trigamma series, and the imaginary part is the unique formal solution of an explicit central-difference equation. Third, we deduce that the coefficients $w_m$ of an explicit even power series attached to the imaginary part satisfy $
u_2(w_m)=-2
u_2((2m)!)$ for every $m\ge0$ ($
u_2$ the $2$-adic valuation). This determines, for every $r$, the exact power of $2$ in the denominator of the coefficient of $\alpha^2$ in the polynomial that represents $\kappa_r$. We also give a factorisation of the amplitude into products of pairs of Gauss functions, further valuation formulas, and a numerical illustration for the zeros.
item.dc:creator: Iv\'an Area

item.title: Wave Packet Density in Local Smoothing: Refinements and Limitations
item.description: arXiv:2609.34675v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study wave packet density estimates in the local smoothing problem for the wave equation. Building on the framework of Gan, He, Li, and Wu, we refine the broad-incidence argument to obtain an improved local smoothing range in even dimensions. We then investigate the limitations of wave packet density methods, showing that genuine geometric obstructions already arise in the Euclidean setting.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyu Wang

item.title: LU-type factorizations and Darboux transformations for continuous-time birth--death processes
item.description: arXiv:2601.14074v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study LU-type factorizations of the infinitesimal generator of a possibly nonconservative birth--death process on $\mathbb{N}_0$, and characterize those for which the corresponding Darboux transformations, obtained by reversing the order of the factors, are again infinitesimal generators of birth--death processes. Two types of factorizations are considered: lower--upper (LU) and upper--lower (UL). In the LU case, the factorization is uniquely determined once the absorption rate of the Darboux-transformed process is fixed, whereas the UL factorization involves an additional free parameter. For both cases we obtain closed-form expressions for the coefficients of the factors in terms of the birth--death rates, determine the exact ranges of the parameters for which the Darboux transforms are birth--death generators, and give probabilistic interpretations of the coefficients in terms of hitting probabilities, expected passage times and occupation times. We also describe the associated spectral transformations (Christoffel and Geronimus transforms) and orthogonal polynomials, and study when the Darboux-transformed process again has a uniquely determined spectral measure: this is always the case for the UL factorization, while for the LU factorization it is characterized by the divergence of a single explicit series. The general results are illustrated with the $M/M/1$ queue, for which all the quantities involved can be computed explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Arcia-Manoleskos, Manuel Dom\'inguez de la Iglesia

item.title: The Corona Problem for Slice Holomorphic Functions via the Matrix Corona Problem
item.description: arXiv:2608.12258v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we prove the Corona theorem for slice hyperholomorphic functions in a general way that applies to functions with values in a Clifford algebra $\mathbb R_n$ for any $n\geq 2$. This general proof is based on a matrix version of Corona's theorem and then exploiting some symmetries of the matrices that allow to reconstruct the values of the functions. The crucial idea is to tie together the algebra of the functions, the Bezout identities and the Carleson-type conditions. The results we obtain rest on a new way of writing the slice product which improves the standard approach and which holds in general dimension.
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Colombo, Elodie Pozzi, Irene Sabadini, Brett D. Wick
